cards.claim: Decorrelated Batch Normalization (DBN) with ZCA whitening improves accuracy on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 compared to standard Batch Normalization
cards.conditions: ResNets/CNNs on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; using ZCA whitening variant; compared against standard BN
cards.effect: Consistent improvement in accuracy (magnitude not specified in excerpt)
cards.evidence: Abstract statement; Section 4.2 experiments on CNNs using CIFAR-10 with VGG-A architecture; Figure 5 shows per-epoch training and test accuracy curves on CIFAR-10
cards.quote: we consistently improve the accuracy of residual networks on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet

cards.claim: ZCA whitening is essential for effective training with decorrelated batch normalization; PCA whitening causes severe training failure due to stochastic axis swapping
cards.conditions: MLPs on MNIST (Figure 2); general neural network training with mini-batch updates
cards.effect: ZCA-whitened activations converge successfully; PCA whitening results in near-random performance (4-layer MLP) or severe degradation
cards.evidence: Experimental results on MLPs (Figure 2); theoretical analysis of stochastic axis swapping problem in Section 3.1
cards.quote: ZCA whitening (referred to as DBN-ZCA) improves training performance significantly compared to no whitening ('plain') and DBN-PCA

cards.claim: Intermediate group sizes for whitening provide better convergence speed than extreme group sizes
cards.conditions: 6-layer MLP on PIE dataset; SGD with batch size 256; group sizes G1, G16, G64, G128
cards.effect: G16 converges significantly faster than G1 or G128; intermediate group sizes show noticeably faster convergence
cards.evidence: Figure 4(a) showing training loss vs iterations; PIE dataset experiments in Section 4.1
cards.quote: the largest (G128) and smallest group sizes (G1) both have noticeably slower convergence compared to the ones with intermediate group sizes such as G16
